parole.significato: An Okinawan stir-fry dish, generally of tofu combined with a vegetable, meat, or fish.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese チャンプルー (chanpurū), from Okinawan ちゃんぷるー (chanpurū), from Malay campur (“to mix”).

parole.significato: An Okinawan martial art involving primarily punching and kicking, but additionally, advanced throws, arm bars, grapplin…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 空(から)手(て) (karate), from 唐(から)手(て) (karate), an orthographic borrowing from Okinawan 唐手(とーでぃー) (tōdī, “Chinese hand”).

parole.significato: A three-stringed instrument of Okinawan origin, the precursor to the shamisen.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 三線 (sanshin) or Okinawan 三線 (sanshin, literally “three strings”). Doublet of sanxian.
